input.quote: 9.8 Any Party shall have the right to review or audit the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs pursuant to this Paragraph 9.
input.rationale: Paragraph 9 (p0160-p0168) is the only regime giving other Parties audit rights over our books and cost records. The right in 9.8 is unlimited in frequency and requires no notice, and 9.9 only channels it through the F&ASC's own audit procedures without supplying either limit — i.e. unlimited, unannounced audits, which is our walk-away position, so this fails the fallback on two material terms. Cost allocation already sits at or above the fallback: under 9.8 the audited Party recovers its entire reasonable compliance costs from the requesting Party, unconditionally and with no underpayment carve-out, so we have not touched it. We have therefore added only the two missing fallback mechanics (once per calendar year; 15 days' prior written notice) as a new 9.10, leaving 9.8 and 9.9 verbatim. The preferred extras (30 days, business hours, independent auditor, off-site preference, no system access) are noted but not pressed, since the audit is mutual and runs to our benefit as auditor as much as against us. Paragraph 10.8's maintenance-records inspection right is a separate, at-own-expense, records-only right with no access to our systems and is not flagged.

proposal.summary: Add annual frequency cap and 15 days' prior written notice to the Paragraph 9 review/audit right
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Paragraph 9 gives any Party an unlimited, unannounced right to review or audit our books, which is our walk-away position. We have added the fallback limits — no more than once in any calendar year and 15 days' prior written notice — and left the existing cost allocation in 9.8 (requesting Party bears the audited Party's compliance costs) and the F&ASC procedure in 9.9 untouched.

ops.text: Any right of review or audit pursuant to this Paragraph 9 shall be exercisable in respect of any Party no more than once in any calendar year, and only upon not less than fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to that Party.

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
mappings.quote: any such Party whose records are being reviewed or audited shall be permitted to recover, from the Party or Parties requesting the review or audit, the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying with the review or audit
